'''Mizuwakasu Shrine''' (水若酢神社, ''Mizuwakasu-jinja'') is a Japanese {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Okinoshima, Shimane|en|Okinoshima, Shimane|qid=Q1205039|lt=Okinoshima|1=Okinoshima, Shimane}}, {{ill|Oki District, Shimane|en|Oki District, Shimane|qid=Q735735|lt=Oki District|1=Oki District, Shimane}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|en|Shimane Prefecture|qid=Q132751|lt=Shimane Prefecture|1=Shimane Prefecture}}. It is a ''[[:en:Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]]''. It is the [[Ichinomiya]] {{ill|Oki Province|en|Oki Province|qid=Q1063829|lt=Oki Province|1=Oki Province}} or the highest ranked shrine in the province.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a">{{Cite web |title=Mizuwakasu Shrine {{!}} List of Geopark Sites and Treasures |url=https://www.oki-geopark.jp/en/geopark-sites-features-list/2694/ |access-date=2023-11-26 |website=Oki Islands UNESCO Global Geopark |language=en-US}}</ref> It is ranked as a [[Beppyo Shrine]], or a special shrine by the [[Association of Shinto Shrines]]. The crest of the shrine has a chrysanthemum symbol.<ref name="水若酢神社-2023a">{{Cite web |date=2023-05-28 |title=水若酢神社（Mizuwakasu Shrine） - shrine-heritager |url=https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |access-date=2023-11-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230528184043/https://shrineheritager.com/en/%E6%B0%B4%E8%8B%A5%E9%85%A2%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88mizuwakasu-shrine%EF%BC%89/ |archive-date=2023-05-28 }}</ref>
It enshrines the deity Mizuwakasu-no-mikoto. This deity is linked to land development in Oki Province and sea protection.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JSMvAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Shinto shrines and festivals |date=1958 |publisher=Association of Shinto Shrines, Kokugakuin University, Institute for Japanese Culture and Classics |language=ja}}</ref>
== History ==
According to legend, the deity rose from the sea, off the shore of Igo, crossed Mt. Ōmine and entered the former Goka Village.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
The shrine might date back to the Kofun Period. This was during {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suijin|1=Emperor Suinin}} or {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|en|Emperor Nintoku|qid=Q313119|lt=Emperor Nintoku|1=Emperor Nintoku}}'s reign.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
In the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]], it was listed as a [[:en:Myōjin Taisha|Myōjin Taisha]] in 927.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=QmdRAAAAYAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Engi-shiki; Procedures of the Engi Era: Books VI-X |date=1972 |publisher=Sophia University |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
The shrine is important in Oki Province. It guards the {{ill|Sea of Japan|en|Sea of Japan|qid=Q27092|lt=Sea of Japan|1=Sea of Japan}}. It appears in the ''[[Shoku Nihongi]]'', a historical text. The ''Inshū Shicho Gakki'', from the [[:en:Edo Period|Edo Period]], mentions it. The {{ill|Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|sv|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari Kokunai Jinmyōchō|qq=}} names it as Mizuwakasu Myojin Oki Ichinomiya Shrine.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
The present [[Honden]] was made in {{ill|1795|en|1795|qid=Q7815|lt=1795|1=1795}}.<ref name="水若酢神社-2023a" />
It was damaged during [[Haibutsu kishaku]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Y5kSAQAAMAAJ&q=Mizuwakasu |title=Business Japan |date=July 1988 |publisher=Nihon Kogyo Shimbun |language=en}}</ref>
== Architecture ==
The shrine's style is unique. The front is ''Yuiitsu Shinmei-zukuri'', like [[Ise Grand Shrine]]. The roof is ''[[Taisha-zukuri]]'', like [[Izumo-taisha|Izumo Grand Shrine]]. The pent roof is ''[[Kasuga-zukuri]]'', like [[:en:Kasuga Grand Shrine|Kasuga Grand Shrine]]. This mix is called ''Oki-zukuri''.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />

== Cultural Status ==
The shrine is designated as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} by the Japanese government.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
== Festivals ==
The grand festival is held on May 3 in odd-numbered years.<ref name="Oki-Islands-UNESCO-Global-Geopark-2023a" />
